# Status

This report covers **Step 1 only**: data download and checks, label verification,
parcellation, coverage and sanity checks. **Step 2 (analyses A–E) was not run.**
Those analyses depend on `connectomeR_0.2.0.tar.gz` (`spin_test()`,
`rotate_parcellation()`, `rewire_degree()`, `node_strength()`, `handle_negative()`, and
the package that the new `R/communication.R` should extend). The tarball was not in the
working folder, the repository, any branch, or anywhere on disk. I did not rewrite the
package from its description, because that would mean inventing code you already have
and validated against the BCT.

Two things in Step 1 need your attention:

1. **No DLB map.** Neither Zenodo record contains a DLB map, links to one or mentions
   Lewy body disease. DLB is left out; no other data were substituted.
2. **The three FTD-variant maps have an unusual scale.** The NIFD variant maps
   (bvFTD, svPPA, nfvPPA) span only about ±1.5–2.0, against −16 to +14 for the pooled
   FTD map from the same cohort. The MINC copies on Zenodo have the same range, so this
   is not a conversion error. The spatial patterns are anatomically sensible (Section 5),
   and every planned analysis is scale-invariant (correlations, ranks, weighted
   neighbour means). So this does not block the analysis, but these values should not
   be read as t-statistics until the authors confirm what was deposited.

# Data

```{r provenance}
source("R/step1.R")
rec <- lapply(c("7392621", "10383493"), function(r)
  jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(paths$zenodo, sprintf("record_%s.json", r))))
files <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rec, function(d) {
  f <- d$files
  f <- f[grepl("Tstat.*\\.nii$", f$key), ]
  data.frame(record = d$doi, file = f$key, md5 = sub("md5:", "", f$checksum))
}))
md5_local <- unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(paths$zenodo, files$file)))
files$md5_ok <- md5_local == files$md5
files
stopifnot(all(files$md5_ok))
dlb_mentioned <- vapply(rec, function(d) grepl("dlb|lewy", tolower(jsonlite::toJSON(d))), TRUE)
dlb_mentioned
```

**Atrophy maps.** Voxel-wise deformation-based morphometry (DBM) t-maps, patients vs
matched controls, on the ICBM152 2009c nonlinear symmetric template.

- Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7392621 (Dadar, 2022; CC-BY-4.0): AD and MCI (ADNI), PD (PPMI),
  pooled FTD (NIFD). The record cites: Dadar M, et al. *White matter hyperintensities
  are associated with grey matter atrophy and cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease
  and frontotemporal dementia.* Neurobiol Aging 2022;111:54–63.
- Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10383493 (Dadar & Metz, 2023; CC-BY-4.0): bvFTD, svPPA,
  nfvPPA (filed as `pnfaPPA`), all NIFD. The record cites Dadar et al. 2022 (above) and
  Metz A, et al. *Brain atrophy and white matter hyperintensities in frontotemporal
  dementia variants and their impact on cognition.* CCNA Partners Forum and Science Days,
  March 2024 (conference presentation).
- Neither record has a DLB map or a link to one (`dlb_mentioned` above is `FALSE` for both).

**Connectomes.** HCP group-level structural (SC) and functional (FC) matrices for
Schaefer-100/200/400 from the ENIGMA toolbox (Larivière et al., Nat Methods 2021),
commit `b08974b`. Only the data files were read.

**Atlas.** Schaefer et al. 2018 (Cereb Cortex), 7-network order, FSL MNI152 1 mm
volumes and label tables from CBIG, commit `634f676`.

`scripts/00_get_data.sh` reproduces every download and checks the md5 sums.

## Image grids

```{r grids}
s1 <- run_step1(write = TRUE)
g <- attr(s1, "grids")
atlas_g <- nifti_grid(file.path(paths$schaefer, "Schaefer2018_400Parcels_7Networks_order_FSLMNI152_1mm.nii.gz"))
grid_tab <- rbind(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(g), function(s) data.frame(
    image = paste0(s, " t-map"), template = "ICBM152 2009c nlin sym",
    dim = paste(g[[s]]$dim, collapse = "×"), voxel_mm = paste(g[[s]]$pixdim, collapse = "×"),
    orientation = g[[s]]$orientation, origin_mm = paste(g[[s]]$affine[1:3, 4], collapse = ", ")))),
  data.frame(image = "Schaefer atlas (all k)", template = "FSL MNI152 (nlin 6th gen)",
             dim = paste(atlas_g$dim, collapse = "×"), voxel_mm = paste(atlas_g$pixdim, collapse = "×"),
             orientation = atlas_g$orientation, origin_mm = paste(atlas_g$affine[1:3, 4], collapse = ", ")))
grid_tab
```

All seven t-maps share one 1 mm grid (`all(attr(s1, "same_grid"))` =
`r all(attr(s1, "same_grid"))`). The atlas is on a different grid and orientation (LAS vs
RAS). It was resampled to the t-map grid by nearest neighbour through world
coordinates; the t-maps were not resampled. The resampling code (`R/parcellate.R`)
returns the atlas unchanged when resampled to its own grid, and gives a result identical
voxel for voxel to an independent nibabel implementation on the t-map grid (checked
during development for Schaefer-400; all 400 labels survive).

The two templates are both "MNI" but not identical (2009c symmetric vs FSL 6th
generation). No transform between them was applied; the residual misregistration is a
few millimetres, which matters little at parcel level but adds to boundary blurring.

## Label order

```{r labels}
label_checks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(resolutions, function(k) {
  info <- read_schaefer_labels(k) # stops with an error if any check fails
  cen <- read.csv(sprintf("data/sphere_centroids_schaefer%d.csv", k))
  data.frame(parcels = k, CBIG_LUT_ids_1toN = TRUE, CBIG_eq_ENIGMA_SC = TRUE,
             CBIG_eq_ENIGMA_FC = TRUE, CBIG_eq_CBIG_centroids = TRUE,
             fsa5_annot_eq_ENIGMA = identical(cen$label, info$label))
}))
label_checks
```

The CBIG label table, the ENIGMA SC and FC label files, the CBIG centroid table and the
ENIGMA fsaverage5 annotation all list the same labels in the same order at 100, 200 and
400 parcels.

## Connectome matrices

```{r matrices}
read_mat <- function(type, k) {
  X <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(paths$enigma_mat, sprintf("%sMatrix_ctx_schaefer_%d.csv", type, k)), header = FALSE))
  dimnames(X) <- NULL; X
}
mat_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(resolutions, function(k) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("struc", "func"), function(ty) {
  X <- read_mat(ty, k); u <- X[upper.tri(X)]
  data.frame(matrix = ifelse(ty == "struc", "SC", "FC"), parcels = k, symmetric = isSymmetric(X),
             diag_zero = all(diag(X) == 0), negative_edges = sum(u < 0), zero_edges = sum(u == 0),
             positive_edges = sum(u > 0), density = round(mean(u != 0), 3),
             min = signif(min(u), 3), max = signif(max(u), 3))
}))))
mat_tab
```

The SC matrices contain `r paste(mat_tab$negative_edges[mat_tab$matrix == "SC"], collapse = ", ")`
negative edges (unique, upper triangle; twice as many entries in the full matrix) at
100, 200 and 400 parcels. In Step 2 they will be set to 0 with
`connectomeR::handle_negative()`. The FC matrices have no negative values; their minimum
is 0, so they appear to have been thresholded upstream.

## Sphere centroids for the spin test

Parcel centroids on the fsaverage5 sphere were computed from the ENIGMA files
(`surfaces/fsa5_sphere_{lh,rh}.gii`, `permutation_testing/annot/fsa5_{lh,rh}_schaefer_*.annot`;
note the annot files are under `enigmatoolbox/permutation_testing/`, not
`datasets/permutation_testing/`). Because `connectomeR/inst/validation/annot_centroids.py`
was not available, `scripts/annot_centroids.py` reimplements the usual method (Vasa et
al. 2018): the mean of each parcel's sphere vertices, snapped to the nearest vertex. The
snapped vertex was the nearest vertex overall for 400/400 parcels. **Compare this file
with the package script before Step 2.**

# Parcellation and coverage

Parcel value = mean t over the parcel's voxels on the t-map grid that have a finite,
non-zero t (the maps are 0 outside their brain mask). Coverage = that voxel count divided
by the parcel's voxel count on the t-map grid. Atrophy is defined as −t.

```{r coverage, fig.height = 3.2}
cov400 <- s1[["400"]]$coverage
cov_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(s1), function(k) {
  cv <- s1[[k]]$coverage
  data.frame(parcels = as.integer(k), min_coverage = round(min(cv$coverage_min), 3),
             median_coverage = round(median(cv$coverage_min), 3),
             parcels_below_50pct = sum(!cv$included),
             coverage_identical_across_maps = all(apply(cv[, grep("^coverage_[A-Za-z]", names(cv))], 1, function(r) diff(range(r)) == 0)))
}))
cov_summary
ggplot(cov400, aes(coverage_min)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.01, fill = col_main, colour = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = 2, colour = "#52514e") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.51, y = Inf, label = "exclusion threshold (50%)", hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, colour = "#52514e") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.45, 1.005), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Voxel coverage (Schaefer-400)", y = "Parcels")
cov400 %>% arrange(coverage_min) %>% head(8) %>%
  transmute(label, n_vox_native, n_vox_grid, coverage = round(coverage_min, 3))
```

No parcel falls below 50% coverage at any resolution, so **no parcels were excluded**.
The least-covered parcels lie at the edge of the t-map brain mask (occipital pole,
LH_Vis_15, 77%; then parcels at the dorsal vertex, 89–93%).

Outputs: `data/parcellated_atrophy_schaefer{100,200,400}.csv`, one row per parcel, with
label, hemisphere, network, CBIG MNI centroid, coverage, an `included` flag and one
atrophy column (−mean t) per syndrome.

# Sanity checks

```{r sanity-tables}
a400 <- s1[["400"]]$atrophy
syn <- names(syndromes)
top_tab <- function(s, n = 10) a400 %>% arrange(desc(.data[[s]])) %>% head(n) %>%
  transmute(rank = row_number(), label = sub("7Networks_", "", label), x = mni_x, y = mni_y, z = mni_z, atrophy = round(.data[[s]], 2))
```

**AD, top 10 parcels (Schaefer-400):**

```{r top-ad}
top_tab("AD")
```

**bvFTD, top 10 parcels:**

```{r top-bvftd}
top_tab("bvFTD")
```

**svPPA and nfvPPA, top 10 parcels:**

```{r top-ppa}
cbind(top_tab("svPPA")[, c("rank", "label", "atrophy")], top_tab("nfvPPA")[, c("label", "atrophy")]) |>
  setNames(c("rank", "svPPA parcel", "svPPA atrophy", "nfvPPA parcel", "nfvPPA atrophy"))
```

The AD map peaks in medial temporal cortex (Limbic_TempPole parcels at y ≈ −20,
z ≈ −27, parahippocampal), lateral and anterior temporal cortex, and the
precuneus/posterior cingulate (Default_pCunPCC). The bvFTD map peaks in the left anterior
insula/frontal operculum (Cont_PFCv_1 at −34, 16, −8; SalVentAttn_FrOperIns), dorsomedial
prefrontal/anterior cingulate (Default_PFCdPFCm) and orbitofrontal cortex (Limbic_OFC).
Both match the expected patterns. Neither map is sign-flipped or empty.

```{r network-profile, fig.height = 6.5, fig.cap = "Mean atrophy (−t) by Schaefer network and hemisphere, Schaefer-400. Each panel has its own x-scale because the FTD-variant maps are on a much smaller scale (see Status)."}
net_order <- c("Vis", "SomMot", "DorsAttn", "SalVentAttn", "Limbic", "Cont", "Default")
prof <- a400 %>% select(hemi, network, all_of(syn)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(syn), names_to = "syndrome", values_to = "atrophy") %>%
  group_by(syndrome, hemi, network) %>% summarise(atrophy = mean(atrophy, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(network = factor(network, rev(net_order)), syndrome = factor(syndrome, syn))
ggplot(prof, aes(atrophy, network, shape = hemi)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#a8a79f", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, colour = col_main, fill = "#fcfcfb", stroke = 0.9) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(LH = 16, RH = 21), name = "Hemisphere") +
  facet_wrap(~syndrome, scales = "free_x", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Mean atrophy (-t)", y = NULL) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The svPPA map is most atrophic in the left, then right, limbic network (temporal
pole). The nfvPPA map is left-lateralized; at network level it is flat across left limbic,
default, salience and dorsal-attention parcels, and its peak parcels are left FEF/premotor,
SMA and anterior insula/IFG (table above). The PD map is weak and diffuse. All
three fit the clinical syndromes.

## Scale of the FTD-variant maps

```{r scale, fig.height = 3.6}
rng <- do.call(rbind, lapply(syn, function(s) {
  img <- as.numeric(RNifti::readNifti(tmap_path(s))); v <- img[img != 0]
  data.frame(syndrome = s, voxel_t_min = round(min(v), 2), voxel_t_max = round(max(v), 2),
             parcel_atrophy_max = round(max(a400[[s]], na.rm = TRUE), 2),
             parcel_atrophy_sd = round(sd(a400[[s]], na.rm = TRUE), 3))
}))
rng
ggplot(a400, aes(FTD, bvFTD)) +
  geom_point(colour = col_main, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
  labs(x = "Pooled FTD atrophy (-t)", y = "bvFTD atrophy (map units)",
       subtitle = sprintf("Same NIFD cohort; r = %.2f across 400 parcels, scale differs by ~%.0f×",
                          cor(a400$FTD, a400$bvFTD), sd(a400$FTD) / sd(a400$bvFTD)))
```

The bvFTD map has the same spatial pattern as the pooled FTD map (r = 0.90), but values
about 8 times smaller in parcel-level SD (about 10 times in voxel range). One possible reading is that the variant maps are standardized
effect sizes or t-values divided by a constant, rather than t-statistics; that is a guess
and should be checked with the authors. It does not affect any planned analysis,
because all of them use correlations, ranks or weighted averages.

# Similarity between syndromes (descriptive)

```{r similarity, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
R <- cor(a400[, syn], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
Rl <- as.data.frame(as.table(R)) %>% setNames(c("a", "b", "r")) %>%
  mutate(a = factor(a, syn), b = factor(b, rev(syn)))
ggplot(Rl, aes(a, b, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 3.2, colour = "#0b0b0b") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = pal_div[["low"]], mid = pal_div[["mid"]], high = pal_div[["high"]],
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Pearson r") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, subtitle = "Schaefer-400. Spin-test p-values pending (need connectomeR::spin_test)") +
  coord_equal() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

These are plain Pearson correlations, without inference. AD resembles MCI (r = 0.80) more
than any FTD map; the pooled FTD map is closest to bvFTD (0.90) and svPPA (0.77); PD is
unrelated to the rest. Spin-test p-values (analysis A) need `spin_test()` from
connectomeR.

# Step 2: not run

Analyses A (spin-test p-values), B (hub susceptibility), C (network-constrained
atrophy with spin and rewiring nulls), D (epicentres) and E (communication models,
including the new `R/communication.R` functions, their bctpy validation and the 0.3.0
version bump) are **not run**. They need the `connectomeR_0.2.0.tar.gz` source package.
Everything they need is in place:

- parcellated atrophy at three resolutions (`data/`), all parcels included;
- verified label order across atlas, matrices, centroid table and annotation;
- fsaverage5 sphere centroids (`data/sphere_centroids_schaefer*.csv`);
- the SC negative-edge counts to report after `handle_negative()`;
- CBIG MNI centroids for the Euclidean distances (navigation and distance baseline);
- bctpy `r sub("bctpy==", "", grep("^bctpy", readLines("output/pip_freeze.txt"), value = TRUE))`
  installed for the validation.

# Limitations (for the full analysis)

- **Different cohorts and pipelines.** AD/MCI come from ADNI, PD from PPMI, and FTD and
  its variants from NIFD. Scanner, acquisition, age, disease stage and control group all
  differ between maps, so cohort effects are mixed with disease effects in any
  between-syndrome comparison. The FTD-variant maps also come from a later deposit with
  a different value scale.
- **Group-level maps.** One map per syndrome means no individual variability and no
  inference across patients; every test is across parcels.
- **Young-adult connectome.** The HCP SC and FC come from healthy adults aged roughly
  22–35, not from older adults or patients.
- **Cortex only.** The Schaefer parcellation omits the hippocampus, amygdala and
  subcortex. For AD (hippocampus) and bvFTD and svPPA (amygdala, striatum, thalamus) the
  likely epicentres sit outside the parcellated cortex; cortical "epicentres" here are at
  best the cortical entry points.
- **DBM signal.** DBM measures local volume change of the deformation, not grey matter.
  Parcel means near CSF can include ventricular or sulcal expansion (positive t). Mean
  t within a parcel also depends on the smoothing used upstream.
- **Template mismatch.** Atlas (FSL MNI152) and maps (ICBM 2009c sym) are on slightly
  different MNI templates; no transform was applied.
- **Spin test.** The parcel-level spin test can be liberal with smooth maps and
  reassigns medial-wall parcels unevenly (Markello & Misic 2021, NeuroImage), so
  degree-preserving rewiring is used as a second null.
- **No DLB.** No DLB map exists in the two records, so Lewy body disease cannot be
  compared.
